ranked.headline: Pretrained biomolecular representations are reused for protein, RNA, and docking tasks
ranked.summary: Recent preprints reuse pretrained protein language models and RNA foundation models across design, fitness, and docking tasks.

ranked.headline: Quantitative frameworks for power, bias correction and mediation in single-cell assays
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and published work provide analytical power formulas and model-based design tools for Perturb-seq and related single-cell experiments.

ranked.headline: Graph-based priors and generative models fuse single-cell, spatial, and bulk omics data
ranked.summary: Multimodal integration now routinely pairs biological graph priors with deep generative or transfer models across unpaired and sparse modalities.

ranked.headline: Interpretable ML links molecular profiles to disease drivers, drugs, and outcomes
ranked.summary: Interpretable models are now being tied to cell-population, molecular, and clinical endpoint readouts across bulk, single-cell, and multi-omics data.

ranked.headline: Single-cell and spatial methods resolve cell-state and communication programmes
ranked.summary: New single-cell, spatial and CRISPR-screen frameworks extend tissue and tumor profiling with explicit cell-state, niche and perturbation models.

ranked.headline: Conserved transcriptomic models read out metabolic health and biological ageing
ranked.summary: Paired single-cell multi-omics and large cross-species atlases now let age and metabolic state be read from transcriptomes across donors and species.

ranked.headline: Joint batch correction and missing-value imputation in single-cell proteomics
ranked.summary: NMFBatch unifies batch correction and missing-data handling for mass spectrometry, while new benchmarks test scRNA-seq methods.

ranked.headline: Long-read workflow choices from sample prep to assembly shape microbial genome recovery
ranked.summary: Long-read sequencing now spans amplicon, metagenomic, and MAG workflows, making end-to-end platform and pipeline choices central to recovery.

ranked.headline: Learned models and structural restraints are resolving protein conformational dynamics
ranked.summary: Experimental restraints, learned models and molecular simulation are now being combined to describe flexibility, disorder and binding in proteins.

ranked.headline: Standardized benchmarks make reliability of spatial and omics inference methods explicit
ranked.summary: Benchmarks such as TADShop and SpatialCCCbench now report method performance explicitly, shifting reliability from assumed to measured.

ranked.headline: Sequence-to-expression models are refined for variant effects and splicing prediction
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs deep sequence models with large experimental and single-cell datasets to test whether predictions generalize beyond training data.

ranked.headline: Sequence foundation models target bacterial gene regulation and metagenomic annotation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pretrain or distill sequence models on microbial data, reporting gains over general genomic and protein language models.

ranked.headline: Comparative genome-wide pipelines expose methodological bias in large-scale inference
ranked.summary: MirMachine 2 applies lineage-aware annotation across thousands of animal genomes and reports methodological bias in its outputs.

ranked.headline: Learned predictors now guide pocket discovery, ADMET triage, and ligand generation
ranked.summary: Blinded multi-company benchmarking of OpenFE and open ADMET datasets are testing predictive models on drug discovery tasks at scale.

ranked.headline: Low-depth and routine sequencing data checked against higher-resolution references
ranked.summary: Recent work tests whether low-depth or routine sequencing reproduces higher-resolution or independent reference measurements.

ranked.headline: New tools for strain, viral and phylogenomic analysis of microbial genomes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published toolkit package strain, phylogenomic and viral classification methods as workflow-ready software.

ranked.headline: Explicit network models test neural mechanisms against connectivity and dimensionality
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published method test neural mechanisms against connectivity, latent structure, and dimensionality measures drawn from data.

ranked.headline: Latent generative models infer hidden single-cell dynamics from static and paired data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair flow matching, optimal transport, and latent causal models to recover temporal and regulatory structure absent from snapshot measurements.

ranked.headline: Simulations link mechanical and membrane conditions to viral entry and antibody binding
ranked.summary: Molecular simulations now resolve how membrane environments, mechanical forces, and mutations shape viral protein function and antibody activity.

ranked.headline: Conformational ensembles explain how single substitutions shift allosteric function
ranked.summary: Recent MD and network analyses link single IP3R1 mutations and an alanine substitution to shifted allosteric communication pathways.

ranked.headline: Sequence-based models infer viral host source, escape risk, and mutation effects
ranked.summary: Viral genomic data now feed quantitative models of host tropism, spillover, immune escape, and vaccine effectiveness directly from sequence.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking normalisation, batch correction and quantification accuracy in omics data
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks and tuning methods formalise how normalisation, machine-learning calibration and batch metrics determine the accuracy of quantitative omics…

ranked.headline: Benchmarks expose leakage and inconsistent evaluation in sequence ML tools
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks and reviews show that ML sequence predictors need standardized evaluation to address leakage and inconsistent reporting.

ranked.headline: Comparison tools for viral genomes, RNA and protein structures, and k-mer sets
ranked.summary: Recent preprints refine alignment, structure comparison, and k-mer indexing to make biological comparisons more sensitive, order-aware, and scalable.

ranked.headline: Improving variant mapping and prioritization beyond standard short-read workflows
ranked.summary: Recent studies address alignment in homologous regions, platform benchmarking against truth sets, and exome variant prioritization.

ranked.headline: Open tools link metabolic networks, lipidomes, and glycan pathways to multi-omics data
ranked.summary: Public atlases and pathway-centered software now make multi-layer metabolic and lipidomic data analyzable beyond specialist users.

ranked.headline: Missing-data-tolerant survival and drug response models across privacy-limited cohorts
ranked.summary: Federated and multimodal methods now address partially overlapping, blockwise missing, and synthetic-data constraints in biomedical prediction.

ranked.headline: Encoding and decoding models probe representational alignment with visual cortex
ranked.summary: Encoding and decoding models now test model-brain correspondence across EEG, fMRI, and MEG, including gradient-level comparisons of vision models.

ranked.headline: Sequence-plus-graph features drive learned prediction of molecular interactions
ranked.summary: Biological language-model features and graph architectures now support interaction prediction across proteins, drugs, and host-virus pairs.

ranked.headline: Explicit structural priors in clinical ML under uncertainty and limited labels
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test whether explicit anatomical or structural information in learners can rival generic architectures in clinical data with limited labels.

ranked.headline: Open computational pipelines are scaling 3D fluorescence and cryo-ET image analysis
ranked.summary: Public microscopy archives and terabyte-scale screens now demand automated tools for tilt estimation, tomogram processing, and organoid imaging data.

ranked.headline: Bayesian and multi-dataset inference refine 13C flux estimates under model uncertainty
ranked.summary: Recent work tackles flux inference under structural uncertainty and multi-dataset fitting, while EnzymeTuning extends enzyme-constrained model accuracy and…

ranked.headline: Automated peak alignment and benchmarking tools advance LC-HRMS metabolomics workflows
ranked.summary: Community benchmarks and new Python tools target peak alignment and MS2 spectral classification in untargeted metabolomics.

ranked.headline: Tools resolving transcript isoforms, polyA sites, and RNA-protein interactions
ranked.summary: Recent tools extend isoform-level annotation across Ribo-seq-supported ORFs, polyA site consensus, and integrated RNA interactomes.

ranked.headline: Deep and feature-based models classify peptides on nanopores and rank MS precursors
ranked.summary: Learned models are being applied to peptide identification and MS target selection beyond conventional sequence-based workflows.

ranked.headline: Population structure and heterogeneity shape evolutionary and epidemic outcomes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published agent-based study examine how graph topology and behavioral or phenotypic heterogeneity alter fixation and spread.

ranked.headline: Structure-based modeling of RNA and PARP1 ligand binding and dataset bias
ranked.summary: RNA-ligand datasets are being cleaned of shortcut bias while simulations map the mechanistic basis of PARP1 inhibitor selectivity.

ranked.headline: Graph and sequence methods are resolving complex diploid and population genomes
ranked.summary: Repeat-rich and complex regions remain hard to assemble and compare, motivating graph-based haplotype and k-mer distance methods.

ranked.headline: Structural variants in parasite genomes shape drug response and population structure
ranked.summary: Pangenome and population-scale structural variant maps now link parasite genome variation to drug response and host adaptation.

ranked.headline: Generative models map protein conformational landscapes from structure and cryo-EM data
ranked.summary: Cryo-EM particle images combined with evolutionary sequence priors now yield continuous atomic-resolution conformational landscapes of protein assemblies.
